key_insight: SCALPEL improves medical image-text alignment by turning a medical LLM into a better encoder and adding anatomy- and negation-aware learning to reduce clinically important mismatches.
clinical_relevance: This could strengthen retrieval, disease classification, and medical visual question answering by making multimodal models more sensitive to details like laterality and negation in radiology reports.
method: Clinical report contrastive fine-tuning adapts a generative LLM into an isotropic text encoder.
An asymmetric alignment design uses offline feature caching to reduce training memory demands.
An anatomy-negation aware loss penalizes image-text mismatches involving laterality confusion and false negations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert, and IU X-Ray across cross-modal retrieval, zero-shot disease classification, and medical VQA.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on high-quality report annotations and careful handling of anatomical laterality/negation during deployment and evaluation.
paper_title: SCALPEL: Semantic Cross-modal Alignment via LLM-Powered Encoder Learning for Medical Vision-Language Representation
